one_line_contribution: A bank-swap protocol that quantifies how much of a reflectively-optimized instruction's gain is bound to the particular experience bank present during optimization, plus a pre-registered head-to-head of five candidate fixes (optimization-time memory masking, shard randomization, deployment-time top-k reduction, bank curation, full re-optimization) with the honest possibility that a deployment-side knob wins and the proposed method is unnecessary.
closest_prior_work: Two threats. (1) MIPROv2 (Opsahl-Ong et al., EMNLP 2024): the proposal dismisses it because the bootstrapped demo set is 'frozen', but MIPROv2's Bayesian search evaluates instruction candidates against *different sampled demonstration sets* across trials and minibatches, which is already exposure to a varying in-context distribution — i.e. the paper's own prescription ('randomize the optimization-time context') is arguably already instantiated in the standard optimizer, and the MIPROv2 demonstration-slot arm is precisely the arm dropped for budget. A reviewer will read that as cutting the comparator that most threatens the contribution. (2) The RAG irrelevant-context-robustness line — RetRobust (Yoran et al., ICLR 2024), Chain-of-Note, RAAT, and FiD-style stochastic document dropping — already establishes that training/prompting under randomized or corrupted retrieved context buys robustness to a changed retrieval distribution. The proposal cites only the FiD-style prior and only as a 'mechanistic prior'. Neither line runs a bank-swap on an *optimized instruction*, so the diagnostic itself survives; but 'instruction evolved against fixed context is brittle to context turnover, and randomizing context during search fixes it' is a corollary a reviewer will regard as already known in substance, which is why the novelty score is low even though the specific measurement is not published.
strongest_objection: D_swap is not identified. D_swap = acc(own bank B_A) − acc(swapped bank B_B) confounds co-adaptation of the instruction to bank content with a plain quality/coverage asymmetry between B_A and B_B, which are built from two different training splits and never counterbalanced (every optimization run in E1 is on split A; only the re-optimization baseline touches B_B, and it never evaluates instr_B on B_A). The design's own logic exposes this: at p=1 the instruction has never seen any bank, so D_swap at p=1 is *by construction* a pure bank-quality difference — yet P1 asserts 'D_swap ≤ 1.5 points at p=1' as a prediction, which is really an untested assumption of bank symmetry smuggled in as a falsifiable claim. Worse, the Stage-1 gate ('proceed only if D_swap at p=0 ≥ 3 points') can be passed by B_B simply being the weaker bank, licensing 33,600 episodes chasing an artifact; and if B_B is the *stronger* bank, real co-adaptation is masked and the study stops at a false bounded null. The hand-written × 3 banks cells contain the correction, but the estimand is never defined as a difference-in-differences, so the headline number and the gate are both stated on the confounded quantity. Compounding this: the setting most likely to make the effect real (ALFWorld / interactive agents, where an ExpeL-style trajectory bank is load-bearing) was cut, and HotpotQA with a 7B model — where distilled 'insights' plausibly move accuracy by well under the 3-point resolution limit — was kept precisely because it is the one that fits the power budget. The most probable outcome of the 21 runs is a bounded null in the setting least likely to exhibit the phenomenon.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Redefine the primary diagnostic as a difference-in-differences: [acc(instr_p, B_A) − acc(instr_p, B_B)] − [acc(hand-written, B_A) − acc(hand-written, B_B)], and restate the Stage-1 gate and P1/P7 thresholds on that quantity, not on raw D_swap. (2) Counterbalance the swap: add >=3 seeds of p=0 optimized on split B and evaluated on B_A, so bank asymmetry is estimated rather than assumed; this is affordable inside the stated envelope by trading the E5 deference-clause arm (6,400 episodes), which is exploratory. (3) Add a same-distribution turnover control B_A' (a resampled/regrown shard of split A) so 'the bank changed' is separated from 'the bank came from different data' — without it, the paper measures split shift, not turnover, and Limitation 8 concedes the abrupt swap is already the maximal case. (4) Select deployment k on a validation split; as written, P8 picks the 'best k in {1,2}' on the same 800 confirmatory items used for the pre-registered test, which contaminates one of the two Bonferroni-protected confirmatory contrasts. (5) Drop or downgrade the 'effect exceeds twice the measured between-seed SD' rule — with 4 seeds the SD estimate has ~3 df and its own CI spans roughly half to double the truth, so this criterion has undefined operating characteristics in a paper whose selling point is measurement rigour; report the mixed-effects interaction CI and the seed-sign agreement instead. (6) Verify the between-seed SD of 1-2 points in the actual pipeline during Stage 1 rather than importing it from a pilot on a different (three-stage cascade) setup; the entire power argument rests on it. (7) Execute and log the dated preprint search before, not after, committing the framing.
missing_baseline: The counterbalanced swap (p=0 instructions optimized on split B, evaluated on B_A) together with a same-distribution bank-refresh control (B_A', a resampled shard of split A). Without these, D_swap cannot be attributed to co-adaptation rather than to B_A/B_B quality asymmetry or to split shift. Secondarily missing: (a) MIPROv2 with its own demonstration resampling as the existing-practice comparator — dropped for budget, yet it is the strongest 'this is already standard' rebuttal; and (b) an irrelevant/random-bank injection cell at each p level, which would show whether D_swap tracks content match at all or is just a function of injected token volume — the pilot's own volume-is-the-lever finding predicts the latter, and E2 only tests volume on the p=0 arm.
preprint_collision: Inadequate, and the proposal says so itself: the check reports that every search call failed and that it has 'zero verified evidence', for the second revision running. By the standard that an unsearched novelty claim is a weakness rather than a neutral, this is a substantial negative, and it is the main reason novelty is scored 4 rather than 6 — a proposal whose central contribution is 'nobody has run this diagnostic' has not attempted to establish that. The listed pre-submission query set is a promise, not evidence, and it arrives too late to inform the design (e.g. if a preprint already reports retrieval-context randomization during prompt search, the E1 grid is the wrong grid, not just a scooped grid). I am likewise restricted from searching here, so I can name only candidate collisions from background knowledge, all unverified: the 2025-2026 agent-memory wave (ReasoningBank, A-MEM, Mem0, Memento and similar) which evaluates learned memory transferred across task distributions and would trivially yield a bank-swap number; DSPy/GEPA robustness and prompt-transfer reports; and the RAG noise-robustness line (RetRobust, Chain-of-Note, RAAT) for the mechanism. The one genuine mitigation is structural and I credit it: restating the contribution as a cost-annotated comparison of five fixes means a preprint that merely names the co-adaptation problem does not scoop the paper. That limits the blast radius; it does not substitute for the search.
